title: Variables
objective: Create, name, and reassign variables correctly.

sourceAlignment.title: Python Crash Course, 3rd Edition
sourceAlignment.author: Eric Matthes
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A variable is a label attached to a value so you can use that value again later. You create one with a single equals sign: the name on the left, the value on the right. Python evaluates the right side first, then attaches the name to the result.

Variable names can use letters, digits, and underscores, but cannot start with a digit and cannot contain spaces. Names are case-sensitive, so score and Score are two different variables. Avoid words Python already uses for something else, like print or if.

A variable can be reassigned at any time. Giving it a new value does not create a second variable — it simply replaces what the name points to, and the old value is gone unless something else was holding onto it.
explanation.rule: name = value creates or updates a variable; the name always points to the most recent value assigned to it.

examples.title: Reassigning a Variable
examples.note: The second assignment replaces the first. Only the newest value remains.

feedback.correct: Correct — letters and underscores, no spaces, no leading digit.
feedback.incorrect: Variable names can't start with a digit and can't contain spaces or hyphens.

assignment.title: Forge Temperature
assignment.brief: Write report_temperature() that stores 1200 in a variable, then prints that variable.
requirements: Create a variable holding the number 1200.
assignment.starterCode:
def report_temperature():
    # Create a variable, then print it.
    pass

report_temperature()
assignment.testHarness:
# ---- Code Forge validation ----
import io, contextlib
_cf_buf = io.StringIO()
with contextlib.redirect_stdout(_cf_buf):
    report_temperature()
_cf_result = _cf_buf.getvalue()
print("__CF_TEST_OUTPUT__")
print(repr(_cf_result))

hints: Pick any valid name, like temperature, and assign it 1200.
Use a single equals sign: name = 1200.
Print the variable name itself, not the number typed again.
The output should just be the number, with no extra text around it.
